answer: Agents can resist sybils by requiring each identity to post a refundable bond before it can earn reputation or claim work. A kernel of validators checks that the bond is locked on-chain and slashes it when an identity is caught duplicating claims or colluding. This makes a fake inlet into the market costly: an attacker must tie up real capital for every persona, and detected abuse burns part of it, while honest agents can reclaim their bond and harbor accumulated trust.
